headline: Apple hikes Mac and iPad prices by hundreds, MacBook Pro now starts at $1,999
summary: Apple has made the unprecedented decision to hike prices across its Mac and iPad lineups, citing rapidly increasing memory and storage costs. The entry-level MacBook Pro jumped $300 to $1,999.
details: Apple has implemented significant price increases across its entire lineup of current MacBooks and iPads. For example, the entry-level MacBook Pro now costs $1,999, a $300 jump, and the MacBook Neo starts at $699 after a $100 hike.

Other models affected include the MacBook Air, now $1,299 (from $1,099), iPad Pro at $1,199 (from $999), and iPad Air at $749 (from $599). The Mac Studio M4 Max mini PC also saw its price increase to $2,499 from $1,999, while iPhone prices remain unchanged.

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple attributed these "unprecedented" price rises to rapidly increasing memory and storage component costs. A company spokesperson stated they had "shielded our customers from these increases so far."

Apple claimed it did all it could to absorb component cost rises, but has now reached a point where price adjustments are necessary. CEO Tim Cook had previously forecast ongoing component shortages and price increases back in April, signaling the challenges ahead.

headline: 83% of EU Crypto Firms to Vacate $78 Billion Market as only 17% are MiCA-Ready
summary: With MiCA enforcement just days away, 83% of registered EU crypto firms lack full authorization and must cease operations by July 1, impacting a significant portion of the $320 billion stablecoin market.
details: With MiCA enforcement just six days away, only 17% of registered EU crypto firms have obtained full authorization. This means 83% of providers must cease EU operations by July 1 or face legal action, according to ainvest.

The EU share of the $320 billion total stablecoin market, with USDC alone at $78 billion, is set to be redistributed. Over 3,000 firms will exit, leaving compliant providers to absorb the significant volume.

For AI agent payment providers, MiCA compliance is critical for continued operation in the EU. Firms that invested in governance infrastructure now hold a structural advantage, as authorization processes typically take 6-12 months, not days.
Post-MiCA, competition shifts from fees and speed to compliance capability. The compliant firms will absorb customers, volume, and margins from those exiting the market.

Developers choosing infrastructure today should prioritize governance-native solutions that produce compliance as a byproduct. This approach ensures every transaction is auditable, every decision traceable, and every record machine-readable for regulators.
